note: Hand-written learning aids, not advice. Each entry says plainly what a term means, why it matters to someone learning the industry, and where to confirm it. An entry is written only where the plain meaning is not in doubt; an entry marked "changing" is a proposal, a threshold or a rule under review, and is shown as a possible meaning needing confirmation rather than as settled. See IMPROVEMENTS.md item 1.

terms.means: the corporate regulator. It licenses financial advice businesses, sets the guidance they work to, and bans people from the industry.
terms.matters: an ASIC action is usually the item that changes what an adviser does, which is why these land as ACT.
terms.check: asic.gov.au

terms.means: the prudential regulator. It supervises banks, insurers and super funds for financial soundness, where ASIC watches conduct.
terms.matters: an APRA item is usually about an institution's stability rather than about advice practice.
terms.check: apra.gov.au

terms.means: the free external complaints scheme. A consumer who cannot resolve a complaint with a firm can take it to AFCA, whose determination binds the firm.
terms.matters: determinations show how obligations are read in a real dispute, which is why they sit in the ACT tier.
terms.check: afca.org.au

terms.means: the tribunal that reviews government decisions, including ASIC bannings. It replaced the Administrative Appeals Tribunal in October 2024.
terms.matters: a ban can be affirmed, varied or set aside here, so an ASIC decision is not always the last word.
terms.check: art.gov.au

terms.means: the tax administrator, and the regulator of self-managed super funds.
terms.matters: it is the primary source for how a tax or SMSF rule is actually applied, ahead of any commentary about it.
terms.check: ato.gov.au

terms.means: the main professional association for advisers, formed in 2023 from the merger of the FPA and the AFA.
terms.matters: it speaks for the profession in consultations. That is a position, not a rule — useful context, rarely an obligation.
terms.check: faaa.au

terms.means: a scheme that pays limited compensation to a consumer who has won an AFCA determination the firm has not paid.
terms.matters: it is funded by a levy on licensees, so changes to how it works change what advice businesses pay.
terms.check: cslr.org.au, and Treasury for any change to the levy

terms.means: the licence a business must hold to provide financial services. An adviser either holds one or is authorised under someone else's.
terms.matters: the licensee carries the obligations, so who holds the licence decides who is answerable.
terms.check: asic.gov.au

terms.means: a person or business authorised to provide financial services under another entity's licence.
terms.matters: it explains why a story about one adviser is often a story about their licensee.
terms.check: asic.gov.au, and ASIC Connect's professional registers

terms.means: an ASIC order stopping a person from providing financial services, or controlling a financial services business, for a set period or permanently.
terms.matters: the reasons given are the closest thing to a worked example of how conduct obligations are applied.
terms.check: the media release and the banning notice at asic.gov.au

terms.means: the legal duty to act in the client's best interests when giving personal advice, in the Corporations Act.
terms.matters: most advice enforcement comes back to it, so it is worth knowing in its own words rather than in summary.
terms.check: the Corporations Act on legislation.gov.au, and ASIC's guidance

terms.means: the ethical standards binding financial advisers, covering competence, honesty, fairness and conflicts of interest.
terms.matters: it sits alongside the law rather than inside it: conduct can meet the Act and still breach the Code.
terms.check: legislation.gov.au for the instrument, asic.gov.au for how breaches are handled

terms.means: the government's package of advice reforms, following the Quality of Advice Review — simplifying advice documents and obligations, and proposing a new class of adviser.
terms.matters: it is the source of most reform talk in the trade press. Much of it is proposed, not law.
terms.check: treasury.gov.au — and confirm whether a measure is announced, in draft, or in force

terms.means: the document that sets out personal advice, the reasons for it, and what it costs.
terms.matters: changes to it are a live reform topic, so check whether a description is current or proposed.
terms.check: treasury.gov.au for reform status, asic.gov.au for what is required today

terms.means: the prohibition on offering a financial product to a consumer during, or because of, unsolicited contact.
terms.matters: it decides how a firm may approach someone who did not ask, including through referrals.
terms.check: the Corporations Act and ASIC's regulatory guidance

terms.means: a payment that could reasonably influence advice given to a client. Most forms of it are banned.
terms.matters: it is the rule behind most stories about commissions and adviser payments.
terms.check: the Corporations Act and ASIC's guidance

terms.means: the obligation on a licensee to report certain breaches, and likely breaches, to ASIC within set timeframes.
terms.matters: the reporting numbers ASIC publishes are where a lot of enforcement attention starts.
terms.check: asic.gov.au regulatory guidance

terms.means: the duty on product issuers and distributors to design a product for a defined group of consumers and distribute it to that group.
terms.matters: it is the obligation behind the target market determination attached to a product.
terms.check: asic.gov.au regulatory guidance

terms.means: the document saying which consumers a financial product is designed for, and how it may be distributed.
terms.matters: distributing outside it is the breach ASIC acts on, so the document is the test.
terms.check: the product issuer's own TMD, and asic.gov.au

terms.means: the disclosure document for a financial product — what it is, its risks, and its costs.
terms.matters: it is the primary source for what a product actually does, ahead of any description of it.
terms.check: the issuer's current PDS

terms.means: a superannuation fund run by its own members, who are also its trustees and carry the legal responsibility.
terms.matters: the trustee obligations, and the ATO's role as regulator, are what separate these from other funds.
terms.check: ato.gov.au

terms.means: a proposed additional tax on earnings attributable to very large superannuation balances.
terms.matters: its thresholds, start date and mechanics have changed more than once. Nothing about it should be taken from a summary.
terms.check: treasury.gov.au and ato.gov.au for the current status — confirm before relying on any figure

terms.means: the obligation on super fund trustees to have a strategy for helping members in retirement, not just while they are saving.
terms.matters: it is why funds have moved into retirement guidance, which touches what advisers do.
terms.check: apra.gov.au and asic.gov.au

terms.means: the supervised year a new adviser completes before advising independently, with structured training and a supervisor.
terms.matters: for someone entering the industry this is the path itself, not background.
terms.check: asic.gov.au and the FAAA's guidance for new entrants

terms.means: the ongoing training an adviser must complete each year to stay authorised.
terms.matters: the requirement is set by law and topped up by the licensee, so counts and categories vary.
terms.check: asic.gov.au, then your licensee's own policy

terms.means: a firm's own complaints process, which a consumer uses before AFCA.
terms.matters: the timeframes and record-keeping are prescribed, and failures here show up in AFCA determinations.
terms.check: asic.gov.au regulatory guidance

terms.means: insurance cover that pays where a person is permanently unable to work, usually to a definition set in the policy.
terms.matters: the definition in the policy decides the claim, and definitions differ between products.
terms.check: the policy document, and the Life Insurance Code of Practice

terms.means: the life insurance industry's own code, with a committee that monitors it and can sanction a breaching insurer.
terms.matters: a code sanction is industry self-regulation, not a regulator's action. Both matter; they are not the same thing.
terms.check: the code at fsc.org.au, and asic.gov.au for anything regulatory

terms.means: a client who meets asset or income tests and so receives fewer protections than a retail client.
terms.matters: the tests, and whether they should change, are a live policy argument. Which category a client is in changes the obligations owed.
terms.check: the Corporations Act, and treasury.gov.au for any review

terms.means: an arrangement where a client's portfolio is managed to a model, with the client holding the underlying assets.
terms.matters: it changes how advice is implemented and reviewed, which is why platform stories dwell on it.
terms.check: the offer document, and asic.gov.au on the licensing of the service

terms.means: the total value of money a manager or platform looks after.
terms.matters: it is a size and momentum figure, not a quality one. Useful as market context, rarely more.
terms.check: the manager's own reporting

terms.means: the tax on a gain made when an asset is sold or otherwise disposed of.
terms.matters: concessions and exemptions do a lot of work here, and they are specific. Never take one from a summary.
terms.check: ato.gov.au
